answer: Physical-Handoff Witness Chain. Each identity must periodically receive a sealed token at a fixed physical site and relay it onward, producing a ripple of handoff timestamps no single operator can fabricate alone. Sites rotate through an orchard of rural pickup points, so travel time bounds how many identities one person can service per day. A sable dye mark on each token, checked at the next site, proves it passed through real hands. An attacker pays roughly four hours of travel per identity per cycle, capping how many agents one operator can sustain.
